title: 2012 AMC 12A Problem 17
statement: Let \(S\) be a subset of \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 30\}\) with the property that no pair of distinct elements in \(S\) has a sum divisible by \(5.\) What is the largest possible size of \(S?\)

solutions.text:
Group \(\{1, \ldots, 30\}\) by residue modulo \(5;\) each class has \(6\) numbers. A sum is divisible by \(5\) when the residues are \(0{+}0,\) \(1{+}4,\) or \(2{+}3.\)

So \(S\) can use at most one number \(\equiv 0,\) and only one of the classes \(\{1\}, \{4\}\) and only one of \(\{2\}, \{3\}.\) That allows at most \(1 + 6 + 6 = 13\) numbers.

The set \(\{1, 2, 6, 7, 11, 12,\) \(16, 17, 21, 22,\) \(26, 27, 30\}\) achieves \(13,\) so the maximum is \(13.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Sort the numbers by their remainder modulo \(5\); there are \(6\) numbers in each class
Residues \(1\) and \(4\) cannot both appear, nor can \(2\) and \(3,\) and at most one multiple of \(5\) is allowed
